content: 1. The oral form of pexidartinib should be administered at least 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid, as aluminum hydroxide decreases the absorption and effectiveness of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. Close monitoring and therapy modification are recommended. 2. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of pindolol by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy closely. 3. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH, which decreases its solubility. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 5. Aluminum hydroxide decreases propranolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 6. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of pseudoephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor therapy, especially with frequent or high-dose antacid use. 7. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 8. Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of quinidine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of ramipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 10. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by interfering with its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids to avoid reduced absorption. Monitor therapy closely. 11. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and plasma concentrations. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For combination products like dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after administration. 12. Magnesium hydroxide reduces riociguat levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. 13. Aluminum hydroxide decreases risedronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 14. Magnesium hydroxide reduces sarecycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair tetracycline absorption, reducing efficacy. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 15. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Aluminum hydroxide reduces rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 17. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of sodium phosphates (IV) by binding cations in the GI tract. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Magnesium reduces serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. Use alternatives if available. 18. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide. Coadministration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 19. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of aluminum hydroxide. Similar risks of adverse events apply. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility. Administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir at least 4 hours apart from antacids. Monitor therapy closely. 21. Aluminum hydroxide reduces sotalol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 22. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its exposure and efficacy. Administer sparsentan 2 hours before or after antacids. Monitor therapy closely. 23. Aluminum hydroxide reduces tiludronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 24. Aluminum hydroxide decreases timolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 25. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of trandolapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of ursodiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Magnesium hydroxide reduces vismodegib levels by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, which reduces bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Vitamin D increases magnesium hydroxide levels by raising serum magnesium concentrations, particularly in patients with renal impairment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Vitamin D increases aluminum hydroxide levels, potentially leading to aluminum retention and toxicity with chronic use. Avoid coadministration. 30. Aluminum hydroxide reduces zoledronic acid levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor therapy. 31. Amikacin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Amiloride increases magnesium hydroxide levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Amphotericin B deoxycholate decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Ascorbic acid increases aluminum hydroxide levels by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Aluminum hydroxide interacts with aspirin, leading to increased salicylate levels at moderate doses and decreased levels at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Aluminum hydroxide interacts with mesalamine, leading to similar salicylate level changes as described above. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Conjugated estrogens decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Furosemide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Magnesium hydroxide decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Paromomycin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Rose hips increase aluminum hydroxide levels by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown.
